children: Gold futures are lower after two days of gains following the U.S. midterm elections, while showing little negative reaction to October's big U.S. payrolls number. Yields and the dollar rise, and while the Fed was already expected to raise interest rates in December, those expectations increased a little. "The metals are lower after two days of a strong snapback rally, although conviction remains weak on either side of the market," Peter Cardillo of Spartan Capital says in a note. Gold for December delivery is off 1% in New York at $4,070.90 a troy ounce. Silver is down 0.7% at $51/98 a troy ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
